reviewer: Independent reviewer (Claude Opus 5 CLI documentation review seat)

fixture.providerMode: dedicated local OpenID Connect fixture; full browser authorization and callback; no external identity-provider account

steps.action: In built-in mode the magic-link switch is locked on with an explanation
steps.actual: With Built-in selected, the Magic-link sign-in switch was present, checked and disabled, and the pane explained that magic links are the only portal sign-in method in built-in mode. The guide statement that the switch cannot turn them off in that mode holds.

steps.action: An existing Business User keeps a live session but cannot get a new link once the domain is removed
steps.actual: Hannah Blum already had an account and a live Portal session at http://127.0.0.1:43328/portal. After northwind.example was removed from Allowed email domains her existing session still reached the Portal, but a fresh Send link request returned the same neutral "Check your email" screen and delivered no message within 8 seconds. Removing a domain therefore stops an existing Business User from obtaining a new sign-in link, which is the correction this review made to both guides. It does not end the session she already holds.

steps.action: Restoring the domain lets the same Business User obtain a link again
steps.actual: Adding northwind.example back restored delivery: the same address received a new sign-in link. The allowlist is read at each request rather than only when an account is first created.

steps.action: An empty allowed-domain list closes the Portal to an existing Business User too
steps.actual: With every entry removed the pane read "No domains allowed yet" and an existing Business User, not merely a new one, could no longer obtain a sign-in link. This is the corrected guide sentence that an empty list admits nobody, verified against an account that already existed. Both domains were added back afterwards.
